newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO under pressure on ample supplies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO under pressure on ample supplies.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil were seen weaker on Thursday with prices coming under pressure from unsold supplies, traders said.
High stocks and unsold supplies would keep a lid on prices in the short term, traders said.
Singapore weekly residues stocks rose by 793,000 barrels in the week ended January 8 to 11 million barrels.
Some traders said there is one more Venezuelan cargo seen heading towards Asia.
Late Thursday, an offer was seen for late January loading supplies at $122 per tonne against no bids.
Discussion were also heard that there are three more South Korean supplies for loading late January that has yet been sold.
In the swaps market, front-month January was last quoted at $119.00/$120.00 per tonne, down about 75 cents from midday, brokers said. Second half January swap traded at $119.50 a tonne, they said.
February was also sold down with deals done at $117.75 and $117.50 a tonne. The market was last quoted at $116.75/$117.75 against $118.50/$119.75 a tonne on Wednesday, brokers said.
